contribution.position: My position is unchanged. The other roles' points on cost, runbook coverage and the run_time figure don't answer the reliability gap. Peak-load run_time is 118s against a 60s budget, and last quarter's two sev2 incidents were both retry storms. A run that overshoots its budget this far can hit timeouts and trigger retries. The passing tests (412 passed, 87% coverage) don't cover load behavior. Closing the gap needs one of three things: retry and timeout settings checked against the 118s figure, a load test showing retry behavior stays bounded, or an explicit waiver or revised budget for the 60s target. Until then the reliability risk is unresolved. The QA claim of 45s conflicts with the 118s peak-load measurement, so the two figures should be reconciled, for example by confirming which load condition each one reflects.
